name: Safety razor
lead: A safety razor is a razor with a guard and a single replaceable double-edge blade held in a reusable handle. It is the design that preceded modern multi-blade cartridges and is favored by wet-shaving enthusiasts.

Many users report a close shave with less irritation and lower blade costs than cartridges. The claim of fewer ingrown hairs is common in forums but is supported mainly by anecdote, and technique matters more than the tool.

paras: The blade protrudes a fixed amount past a guard, cutting hair at the skin surface while limiting depth. A single blade avoids the tug-and-cut action of multi-blade cartridges that may pull hairs below skin level.

Dermatology reviews on shaving bumps recommend softening hair first, not stretching the skin, avoiding very close passes and using a lubricating gel, regardless of razor type. Single-blade razors can still cut or irritate with poor technique and can nick skin. Independent head-to-head trials against cartridges are lacking, so the stronger rating is based on practicality, and sensitivity varies by person.
